- Expected steady-state: ~700k tokens/day (mostly requests ~30–200 tokens).

Asks from our side to finalize an estimate:

2) Which flows MUST meet the 250 ms p99? (e.g., login assist vs background enrichment)
3) Any regulatory constraints for data residency or key management?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share a short multipath recommendation (streaming vs batch, model tiering) and an XLS with unit econ scenarios — attaching PoC scope and the estimate.

Hi Asha — looping Marissa (SE) into the thread — she has the deeper perf numbers. Below are quick scenarios that match your ~$60–$80 / 1M token target and the latency SLO split you described. Attached: redwood-multipath-estimate.xlsx with three bands (conservative / baseline / aggressive).

TL;DR recommendations
- Start PoC with a two-path setup:
  1) Interactive path (streaming, small quantized model variant) — preserves low p99; smaller model reduces inference time and KV overhead.
  2) Bulk path (batched, slightly larger/quantized model) — runs async enrichment jobs at higher throughput and much lower $/1M tokens.
- Canary dedicated pool: reserve 3 GPUs (mid-tier) with autoscale burst for spikes.

Unit economics (baseline example, approximate):
- Baseline band: $72 / 1M tokens — streaming priority for 30% of tokens (interactive), batching for 70% (background).
- Aggressive quantization + more batching: ~$48–$58 / 1M tokens (ratchet up cache reuse and continuous batching).
- If you require p99 ≤250ms for 100% of tokens, unit cost moves up ~25–40% because batching headroom reduces.

Key trade-offs (short):
- Streaming: best p99, lower batching efficiency → higher $/token. Good for bursts and interactive UX.
- Aggressive batching: best $/token, higher p99 tail unless you isolate interactive flows.
- Model tiering (small for interactive, medium for bulk) often gives the best composite economics.

Attachments: redwood-multipath-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet with per-band math)

I’ll let Marissa add the perf numbers and a suggested GPU count for the canary. If this looks like the right framing, we can convert the baseline sheet into an official quote and SOW.

Best,
Rishi

Hi Asha — quick technical addendum to Rishi's note with concrete perf/cost guidance.

Performance notes and recommended config:
- Interactive (p99 target ≤250 ms)
  - Approach: streaming inference on a quantized 7B-class variant; enable prefix KV caching and per-connection warmup.
  - Expected p50/p90/p99 on mid-tier GPU: ~45 ms / 120 ms / 220–260 ms (depends on input length distribution).
  - Cost implication: streaming for interactive flows reduces batching efficiency; expect ~1.3–1.6x cost multiplier vs fully batched tokens.

- Bulk enrichment (relaxed SLO ~1s)
  - Approach: continuous batching with larger batches and mixed-precision quantization. Use model tier that gives better per-token compute efficiency.
  - Expected throughput: 40–60M tokens/day per 3-GPU pool under continuous batching conditions.
  - Cost implication: fully batched path can get you down to ~$30–$45 / 1M tokens depending on model/quantization.

Multipath orchestration recommendations:
- Traffic routing: use policy-based routing (latency-first for interactive, cost-first for enrichment).
- Canary sizing: start with 3 reserved GPUs + burst to 5 for peak hours. Observe prefix hit rates and adjust batch windows.
- Monitoring: enable token-level cost dashboards and p99 tracing for the interactive routes; set auto-fallback to a slightly cheaper model for non-critical flows.

Example math (baseline assumptions):
- 30M tokens/month total: 9M interactive (streaming), 21M batched.
- Streaming path cost: 9M tokens * ($0.000072 per token equivalent) ≈ $648 (apportioned to $72 / 1M tokens for the interactive fraction).
- Batched path cost: 21M tokens at ~$35 / 1M ≈ $735.
- Combined ≈ $1,383 => ~ $46 / 1M blended (note: numbers vary by model and reserved vs on-demand pricing).

Next steps from SE side:
1) If Helix confirms the 3-band target (conservative/baseline/aggressive), I’ll produce a short SOW and per-band quote we can pass to procurement.
2) Technical kickoff: 30–45 min canary design call to lock GPU types and sample prompt suite.

Happy to join the procurement call if you need an SLA/technical appendix.

Thanks,
